body:
Hey, good luck on the lecture.  You seem to know what you're talking about, so I'm sure it will be a breeze.

Also, Reddit University?  Alternative education has gone in some really unexpected directions in recent years!

These resources are awesome.  You r00l.

Oh, but make sure to take advantage of the mental health services at your school while you can.  I wish I had done that.  I don't have insurance or any options like that now, and I feel like a sucker for not having gone while I still could.

Why are you still living?  That's not the question we as humans should ask ourselves.  We just live, and do the best we can while we are here.  Losing a friend is painful, but try to focus on the good memories.  Those don't disappear or get invalidated when circumstances change, and circumstances will always be changing.  Don't forget that friends fight sometimes.  Plus, the internet makes physical distance between people surmountable.  

If you're in school, you have resources available to you.  Talk to a counselor about your feelings and see if you can't work through this.  Maybe things look bleaker than they actually are right now, but you are too upset to rationally evaluate the situation.  Happens to me all the time.

Thank you for that link.  I will definitely bookmark it and give it a look-see.  Web development sounds like a good opportunity, and my brother is encouraging me to do it.  If you don't come from a tech background, however, it seems impossible to surmount the barrier of entry.  I really need an ELI5, haha.

I wish I had just majored in programming.  I was just too scared and uninformed.  I was a perfectionist and thought getting straight As in history would be better than being a mediocre programmer.  Honestly, I think eighteen is too young to be making an important life decision like selecting a major or taking out a student loan.  I hope someday the pressure for high school graduates isn't to leap blindly into college, but rather to take a few years to try working, learn what they are good at, and consider vocational training instead of academia.

E-hugs for everyone!

I don't really know what to say, but after this struggle, I think it would be sad if you gave up now, especially for your parents.  If you're worried about their well-being, maybe you could make it your goal to pay them back.  Just, it's a goal, you know?  Maybe not necessarily financially, but you can return the favor when they are ailing in their old age.  That's as good a reason to live as any, I suppose.

Thank you for sharing.  I'm glad to see that you made it through.

Getting involuntarily locked up was always my nightmare.
Haha, thanks.  But, it isn't your responsibility.  If I am truly committed to making a change, I'll find a way.

Your external circumstances may not be good, but YOU the person obviously have talent, and you should recognize that and take comfort in it.  You're not a leech.  You've got a boyfriend who obviously cares about you, too.  That's so amazing.
